reading: Three colour bands per row: left colour, a middle-colour run, then the rest. Each row's middle run slides left so its right end sits on the shape's minimum right-end column (clamped at column 0); the left colour fills the vacated cells behind it.

slots.subject: the middle-colour run of each row (colour right after the left band)
slots.target column: the smallest right-end column of the middle colour over all rows
slots.filler: the left-band colour fills cells vacated up to the run's old right end
slots.rest: background and the third colour unchanged

why: per row, middle-run length and left-colour count are preserved; middle run ends at min right-end column unless it would pass column 0

reading: Two rectangles; one carries a one-cell-wide stem of its own colour that reaches the other. The stem is erased and the stemmed rectangle slides along the stem direction until it touches the other rectangle.

slots.mover: the rectangle body of the object that has a one-cell-wide stem
slots.stem: the 1-wide line cells, cleared to background
slots.direction: along the stem toward the anchor, until adjacent

why: mover keeps its rectangle shape, ends in contact with the anchor, stem cells disappear, anchor unchanged

reading: Input is three 4x4 panels of 5 split by background columns; each panel's hole pattern maps to a colour (solid->2, centre 2x2 hole->8, bottom-centre hole->4, side holes in middle rows->3). Output row i is filled with panel i's colour.

slots.panels: three 4x4 panels cut by all-background columns
slots.key: hole pattern -> colour: solid 2, centre hole 8, bottom hole 4, left/right holes 3
slots.output: 3x3 grid, row i uniform with panel i's colour

why: each output row is one colour equal to the class of the corresponding panel
invariants: one row per panel, left-to-right order -> top-to-bottom

reading: Each isolated coloured cell draws a line rightward to the right border, then down the last column until the row just above the next marker's row (or to the bottom for the last marker).

slots.source: markers (isolated cells), taken in row order
slots.path: right to the border, then down along the last column
slots.stop: the row before the next marker's row, else the bottom border

why: every marker row is filled from the marker to the right edge; the last column between marker rows takes the colour of the marker above

reading: A frame made of four coloured sides (corners empty) and a separate 8-shape sized to its interior. Output is the frame cut out with the 8-shape placed inside; each 8 cell takes the colour of the nearest side, and stays 8 when two sides tie.
verb: insert shape into frame, colour by nearest side

slots.container: the four-sided frame (top, bottom, left, right one-colour bars), cropped to its box
slots.content: the 8 object, placed so its box fills the frame interior
slots.key: nearest frame side by distance; tie -> keep 8

why: output = frame box; interior cells empty where shape empty, else nearest-side colour or 8 on ties

reading: Count each colour's cells; output has one column per colour ordered by count (largest first), each column filled from the top with as many cells as that colour's count, rest 0. Height = largest count.

slots.bars: one per input colour, sorted by descending cell count

why: column j has exactly count(colour j) cells of colour j at the top, counts non-increasing left to right

reading: The grid is two solid colour regions (8 and 1) holding 2-blocks. Within each region the 2 cells of every row slide horizontally to the region's edge: left in the 8 region, right in the 1 region.
why: per panel (colour region, not separator-cut), 2 cells per row are preserved and packed against the panel border; direction fixed by panel colour (8->left, 1->right)
invariants: number of 2 cells per row per panel

reading: Two framed regions each contain rectangles with one-cell defects: a notch (frame colour poking in) or a bump (rectangle colour poking out). Each defect becomes a 2-cell stroke across the rectangle edge (the defect cell plus its neighbour on the other side), coloured with the other framed region's colour.

slots.defects: single cells on a rectangle's edge that break its outline (notch or bump)
slots.stroke: defect cell plus the adjacent cell across the edge (outward for a notch, inward for a bump)
slots.colour: the colour of the other big framed region (the two regions swap colours)

why: every changed cell lies on a 1x2 stroke straddling a rectangle edge at a defect; nothing else changes

reading: Colour-3 cells slide left along their row through background until they hit an 8 or the left border; each row moves independently.
why: parts = each row's horizontal run of 3; it keeps its length and ends touching an 8 (or the border) on its left

reading: On a 5/0 noise field, a few 3x3 windows contain only 2 and 5 cells with all touching 2-components inside the window (centre not 2). In each such window the centre becomes 4 and every 5 becomes 7; 2 cells stay.

slots.windows: 3x3 blocks with no 0, at least one 2, centre not 2, and every 2-component they touch lying fully inside (on overlap, the window holding more 2s)

why: every changed cell is 5->7 or centre 5->4 inside a selected window; four windows per pair
